"""Error model and duplicate filtering for Pylama."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import Any, DefaultDict, Dict, Iterable, List, Set, Tuple

PATTERN_NUMBER = re.compile(r"^\s*([A-Z]\d+)\s*", re.I)

_DUPLICATE_GROUPS = (
    {("pycodestyle", "E701"), ("pylint", "C0321")},
    {("pylint", "W0612"), ("pyflakes", "W0612")},
    {("pylint", "E0602"), ("pyflakes", "E0602")},
    {("pylint", "W0611"), ("pyflakes", "W0611")},
    {("pylint", "C0326"), ("pycodestyle", "E202")},
    {("pylint", "C0326"), ("pycodestyle", "E211")},
    {("pylint", "C0326"), ("pycodestyle", "E222")},
    {("pylint", "C0326"), ("pycodestyle", "E225")},
    {("pylint", "C0326"), ("pycodestyle", "E251")},
    {("pylint", "C0301"), ("pycodestyle", "E501")},
    {("pylint", "W0301"), ("pycodestyle", "E703")},
    {("pylint", "C0321"), ("pycodestyle", "E702")},
    {("pylint", "W0311"), ("pycodestyle", "E111")},
    {("pylint", "W0401"), ("pyflakes", "W0401")},
    {("pydocstyle", "D100"), ("pylint", "C0111")},
)

DUPLICATES: Dict[Tuple[str, str], Set[Tuple[str, str]]] = {
    key: set(group) - {key}
    for group in _DUPLICATE_GROUPS
    for key in group
}


class Error:
    """Store error information from a linter."""

    __slots__ = ("source", "col", "lnum", "etype", "message", "filename", "number")

    def __init__(
        self,
        source: str = "pylama",
        col: int = 1,
        lnum: int = 1,
        type: str | None = None,
        text: str = "unknown error",
        filename: str = "",
        number: str = "",
        **_,
    ):
        text = str(text).strip().replace("\n", " ")
        if not number:
            match = PATTERN_NUMBER.match(text)
            number = match.group(1).upper() if match else ""
        self.number = number
        self.etype = type[:1] if type else (number[:1] if number else "E")
        self.col = max(int(col or 1), 1)
        self.filename = str(filename)
        self.source = source
        self.lnum = int(lnum or 1)
        self.message = text

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        return self.message

    @property
    def type(self) -> str:
        return self.etype

    def __getitem__(self, key: str) -> Any:
        return self.to_dict()[key]

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"<Error:{self.lnum}:{self.col}: {self.number} {self.message}>"

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.filename}:{self.lnum}:{self.col}: {self.number} {self.message} ({self.source})"

    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        if not isinstance(other, Error):
            return NotImplemented
        return (
            self.filename,
            self.lnum,
            self.col,
            self.number,
            self.message,
            self.etype,
            self.source,
        ) == (
            other.filename,
            other.lnum,
            other.col,
            other.number,
            other.message,
            other.etype,
            other.source,
        )

    def format(self, pattern: str) -> str:
        return pattern.format(
            filename=self.filename,
            lnum=self.lnum,
            col=self.col,
            message=self.message,
            text=self.message,
            etype=self.etype,
            type=self.etype,
            source=self.source,
            number=self.number,
        )

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "source": self.source,
            "col": self.col,
            "lnum": self.lnum,
            "etype": self.etype,
            "type": self.etype,
            "message": self.message,
            "text": self.message,
            "filename": self.filename,
            "number": self.number,
        }


def remove_duplicates(errors: Iterable[Error]) -> List[Error]:
    """Filter duplicate errors reported by multiple linters."""
    unique: List[Error] = []
    passed: DefaultDict[Tuple[str, int], Set[Tuple[str, str]]] = defaultdict(set)
    for error in errors:
        location = (error.filename, error.lnum)
        key = (error.source, error.number)
        if key in passed[location]:
            continue
        if key in DUPLICATES and passed[location] & DUPLICATES[key]:
            continue
        passed[location].add(key)
        unique.append(error)
    return unique


def default_sorter(err: Error) -> Any:
    """Sort by line number."""
    return err.lnum

"""VCS hooks for Pylama."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from configparser import ConfigParser
from os import chmod, getcwd
from os import path as op
from subprocess import PIPE, Popen
from typing import List, Tuple

from pylama import LOGGER
from pylama.config import parse_options, setup_logger
from pylama.main import check_paths, display_errors


def run(command: str) -> Tuple[int, List[bytes], List[bytes]]:
    """Run a shell command and capture output."""
    with Popen(command.split(), stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE) as pipe:
        stdout, stderr = pipe.communicate()
        return (
            pipe.returncode,
            [line.strip() for line in stdout.splitlines()],
            [line.strip() for line in stderr.splitlines()],
        )


def git_hook(complexity: int = -1, strict: bool = False, linters: str = "pycodestyle,mccabe,pyflakes", error=None) -> int:
    """Run Pylama against staged files in a Git repository."""
    if error is not None:
        strict = bool(error)
    _, files_modified, _ = run("git diff-index --cached --name-only HEAD")
    overrides = {"linters": linters}
    if complexity >= 0:
        overrides["max_complexity"] = complexity
    options = parse_options(**overrides)
    setup_logger(options)
    candidates = [file_.decode("utf-8") for file_ in files_modified]
    if not candidates:
        return 0
    errors = check_paths(candidates, options, rootdir=Path(getcwd()))
    display_errors(errors, options)
    return int(strict and bool(errors))


def hg_hook(_, repo, node=None, **kwargs):
    """Run Pylama after a Mercurial commit."""
    del kwargs
    candidates = []
    seen = set()
    try:
        if len(repo):
            start = repo[node] if node is not None else 0
            for rev in range(start, len(repo)):
                for file_ in repo[rev].files():
                    filename = op.join(repo.root, file_)
                    if filename in seen or not op.exists(filename):
                        continue
                    seen.add(filename)
                    candidates.append(filename)
    except Exception:
        return False
    options = parse_options()
    setup_logger(options)
    if candidates:
        errors = check_paths(candidates, options)
        display_errors(errors, options)
        return bool(errors)
    return False


def install_git(path):
    """Install a Git pre-commit hook."""
    hook = op.join(path, "pre-commit")
    with open(hook, "w", encoding="utf-8") as target:
        target.write(
            """#!/usr/bin/env python
import sys
from pylama.hook import git_hook

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(git_hook(strict=True))
"""
        )
    chmod(hook, 0o744)


def install_hg(path):
    """Install Mercurial hooks."""
    hook = op.join(path, "hgrc")
    if not op.isfile(hook):
        open(hook, "w+", encoding="utf-8").close()
    cfgp = ConfigParser()
    with open(hook, "r", encoding="utf-8") as source:
        cfgp.read_file(source)
    if not cfgp.has_section("hooks"):
        cfgp.add_section("hooks")
    if not cfgp.has_option("hooks", "commit"):
        cfgp.set("hooks", "commit", "python:pylama.hook.hg_hook")
    if not cfgp.has_option("hooks", "qrefresh"):
        cfgp.set("hooks", "qrefresh", "python:pylama.hook.hg_hook")
    with open(hook, "w+", encoding="utf-8") as target:
        cfgp.write(target)


def install_hook(path):
    """Auto-detect the VCS and install the appropriate hook."""
    is_git = op.join(path, ".git", "hooks")
    is_hg = op.join(path, ".hg")
    if op.exists(is_git):
        install_git(is_git)
        LOGGER.warning("Git hook has been installed.")
        return 0
    if op.exists(is_hg):
        install_hg(is_hg)
        LOGGER.warning("Mercurial hook has been installed.")
        return 0
    LOGGER.error("VCS has not found. Check your path.")
    sys.exit(1)

/workspace/README.rst.content:
Pylama
======

Pylama is a Python code audit tool that runs multiple linters behind a single
CLI and API.

Features
--------

* Unified interface for `pycodestyle`, `pyflakes`, `mccabe`, `pydocstyle`,
  `pylint`, `mypy`, `isort`, `eradicate`, `vulture`, and `radon`
* INI and TOML configuration support
* Recursive path scanning and stdin support
* Multiple output formats, including JSON
* Optional concurrent checking for large code bases

Basic usage::

    pylama package_name
    pylama --linters=pycodestyle,pyflakes,mccabe module.py
    python -m pylama --from-stdin virtual.py < code.py

"""Pylama core execution."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os.path as op
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List

from pylama import LOGGER
from pylama.config import CURDIR, Namespace
from pylama.context import RunContext
from pylama.errors import Error, default_sorter, remove_duplicates
from pylama.lint import LINTERS, LinterV2


def run(
    path: str,
    code: str = None,
    rootdir: Path = CURDIR,
    options: Namespace = None,
) -> List[Error]:
    """Run all configured linters against one file."""
    path = op.relpath(path, rootdir)
    with RunContext(path, code, options) as ctx:
        if ctx.skip:
            LOGGER.info("Skip checking for path: %s", path)
        else:
            for linter_name in ctx.linters or list(LINTERS):
                linter_cls = LINTERS.get(linter_name)
                if not linter_cls:
                    continue
                linter = linter_cls()
                LOGGER.info("Run [%s] %s", linter_name, path)
                if hasattr(linter, "allow") and not linter.allow(Path(ctx.filename)):
                    continue
                if isinstance(linter, LinterV2):
                    linter.run_check(ctx)
                else:
                    for err_info in linter.run(
                        ctx.temp_filename,
                        code=ctx.source,
                        params=ctx.get_params(linter_name),
                    ):
                        ctx.push(source=linter_name, **err_info)
    if not ctx.errors:
        return ctx.errors
    errors = remove_duplicates(ctx.errors)
    sorter = default_sorter
    if options and options.sort:
        sort = options.sort
        sorter = lambda err: (sort.get(err.etype, 999), err.lnum)
    return sorted(errors, key=sorter)

"""radon integration."""

from __future__ import annotations

from argparse import ArgumentError, ArgumentParser

from radon.complexity import add_inner_blocks
from radon.visitors import ComplexityVisitor

from pylama.context import RunContext
from pylama.lint import LinterV2 as Abstract


class Linter(Abstract):
    """radon runner."""

    name = "radon"

    @classmethod
    def add_args(cls, parser: ArgumentParser):
        parser.add_argument(
            "--radon-no-assert",
            default=False,
            action="store_true",
            help="Ignore assert statements.",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--radon-show-closures",
            default=False,
            action="store_true",
            help="Increase complexity on closures.",
        )
        try:
            parser.add_argument(
                "--max-complexity",
                default=10,
                type=int,
                help="Max complexity threshold.",
            )
        except ArgumentError:
            pass

    def run_check(self, ctx: RunContext):
        params = ctx.get_params("radon")
        options = ctx.options
        if options:
            params.setdefault("complexity", options.max_complexity)
            params.setdefault("no_assert", getattr(options, "radon_no_assert", False))
            params.setdefault("show_closures", getattr(options, "radon_show_closures", False))

        complexity = int(params.get("complexity", 10))
        no_assert = params.get("no_assert", False)
        show_closures = params.get("show_closures", False)
        visitor = ComplexityVisitor.from_code(ctx.source, no_assert=no_assert)
        blocks = add_inner_blocks(visitor.blocks) if show_closures else visitor.blocks
        for block in blocks:
            if block.complexity > complexity:
                ctx.push(
                    lnum=block.lineno,
                    col=block.col_offset + 1,
                    source="radon",
                    type="R",
                    number="R901",
                    text=f"{block.name} is too complex {block.complexity}",
                )

from __future__ import annotations

from pyflakes import checker

from pylama.context import RunContext
from pylama.lint import LinterV2 as Abstract

m = checker.messages

CODES = {}
_MESSAGE_CODES = {
    "UnusedImport": "W0611",
    "RedefinedWhileUnused": "W0404",
    "ImportShadowedByLoopVar": "W0621",
    "ImportStarUsed": "W0401",
    "ImportStarUsage": "W0401",
    "ImportStarNotPermitted": "W0401",
    "UndefinedName": "E0602",
    "DoctestSyntaxError": "W0511",
    "UndefinedExport": "E0603",
    "UndefinedLocal": "E0602",
    "DuplicateArgument": "E1122",
    "LateFutureImport": "W0410",
    "FutureFeatureNotDefined": "W0410",
    "UnusedVariable": "W0612",
    "UnusedAnnotation": "W0612",
    "UnusedIndirectAssignment": "W0612",
    "ReturnOutsideFunction": "E0104",
    "BreakOutsideLoop": "E0103",
    "ContinueOutsideLoop": "E0103",
    "DefaultExceptNotLast": "E0701",
    "RaiseNotImplemented": "E0711",
}
for name, code in _MESSAGE_CODES.items():
    if hasattr(m, name):
        CODES[getattr(m, name).message] = code


class Linter(Abstract):
    """Pyflakes runner."""

    name = "pyflakes"

    def run_check(self, context: RunContext):
        params = context.get_params("pyflakes")
        builtins = params.get("builtins", "")
        if builtins:
            if isinstance(builtins, str):
                builtins = [item for item in builtins.split(",") if item]
            else:
                builtins = list(builtins)

        check = checker.Checker(context.ast, context.filename, builtins=builtins)
        for msg in check.messages:
            text = msg.message % getattr(msg, "message_args", ())
            column = getattr(msg, "col", 0) or 0
            context.push(
                lnum=getattr(msg, "lineno", 1),
                col=column + 1,
                text=text,
                number=CODES.get(msg.message, ""),
                source="pyflakes",
            )

"""vulture integration."""

from __future__ import annotations

from argparse import ArgumentParser

from vulture.core import ERROR_CODES, Vulture, make_config

from pylama.context import RunContext
from pylama.lint import LinterV2 as BaseLinter


class Linter(BaseLinter):
    """vulture runner."""

    name = "vulture"

    @classmethod
    def add_args(cls, parser: ArgumentParser):
        parser.add_argument(
            "--vulture-min-confidence",
            type=int,
            help="Minimum confidence for code to be reported as unused.",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--vulture-ignore-names",
            help="Comma-separated list of names to ignore.",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--vulture-ignore-decorators",
            help="Comma-separated list of decorators to ignore.",
        )

    def run_check(self, ctx: RunContext):
        params = ctx.get_params("vulture")
        options = ctx.options
        if options:
            params.setdefault("min-confidence", getattr(options, "vulture_min_confidence", None))
            params.setdefault("ignore-names", getattr(options, "vulture_ignore_names", None))
            params.setdefault(
                "ignore-decorators",
                getattr(options, "vulture_ignore_decorators", None),
            )

        config = make_config(parse_params(ctx.filename, params))
        vulture = Vulture(
            verbose=config["verbose"],
            ignore_names=config["ignore_names"],
            ignore_decorators=config["ignore_decorators"],
        )
        vulture.scan(ctx.source, filename=ctx.filename)
        unused_code_items = vulture.get_unused_code(
            min_confidence=config["min_confidence"],
            sort_by_size=config["sort_by_size"],
        )
        for item in unused_code_items:
            error_code = ERROR_CODES[item.typ]
            ctx.push(
                source="vulture",
                type="R",
                lnum=item.first_lineno,
                number=error_code,
                text=f"{item.message} ({item.confidence}% confidence)",
            )


def parse_params(path, params=None):
    """Convert params from Pylama to vulture CLI arguments."""
    params = params or {}
    return [f"--{key}={value}" for key, value in params.items() if value] + [path]

"""pycodestyle integration."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pycodestyle import BaseReport, Checker, StyleGuide, get_parser

from pylama.context import RunContext
from pylama.lint import LinterV2 as Abstract


class Linter(Abstract):
    """pycodestyle runner."""

    name = "pycodestyle"

    def run_check(self, ctx: RunContext):
        params = ctx.get_params("pycodestyle")
        options = ctx.options
        if options:
            params.setdefault("max_line_length", options.max_line_length)

        if params:
            parser = get_parser()
            for option in parser.option_list:
                if option.dest and option.dest in params:
                    value = params[option.dest]
                    if isinstance(value, str):
                        params[option.dest] = option.convert_value(option, value)

        style = StyleGuide(reporter=_PycodestyleReport, **params)
        report_options = style.options
        report_options.report.ctx = ctx  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        checker = Checker(ctx.filename, lines=ctx.lines, options=report_options)
        checker.check_all()


class _PycodestyleReport(BaseReport):
    """Capture pycodestyle errors into the current context."""

    ctx: RunContext

    def error(self, line_number, offset, text, _):
        code, _, message = text.partition(" ")
        self.ctx.push(
            text=message,
            type=code[0],
            number=code,
            col=offset + 1,
            lnum=line_number,
            source="pycodestyle",
        )

"""pydocstyle integration."""

from __future__ import annotations

from argparse import ArgumentParser

from pydocstyle import ConventionChecker as PyDocChecker
from pydocstyle.violations import conventions

from pylama.context import RunContext
from pylama.lint import LinterV2 as Abstract


class Linter(Abstract):
    """pydocstyle runner."""

    name = "pydocstyle"

    @classmethod
    def add_args(cls, parser: ArgumentParser):
        parser.add_argument(
            "--pydocstyle-convention",
            choices=list(conventions.keys()),
            help="Choose a predefined docstring convention.",
        )

    def run_check(self, ctx: RunContext):
        params = ctx.get_params("pydocstyle")
        options = ctx.options
        if options and getattr(options, "pydocstyle_convention", None):
            params.setdefault("convention", options.pydocstyle_convention)
        convention_codes = conventions.get(params.get("convention"))
        for err in PyDocChecker().check_source(
            ctx.source,
            ctx.filename,
            params.get("ignore_decorators"),
            params.get("property_decorators"),
            params.get("ignore_inline_noqa", False),
            params.get("ignore_self_only_init", False),
        ):
            if convention_codes is None or err.code in convention_codes:
                ctx.push(
                    lnum=err.line,
                    text=err.short_desc,
                    type="D",
                    number=err.code,
                    source="pydocstyle",
                )

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import Any, DefaultDict, Dict, Iterable, List, Set, Tuple

PATTERN_NUMBER = re.compile(r"^\s*([A-Z]\d+)\s*", re.I)

_DUPLICATE_GROUPS = (
    {("pycodestyle", "E701"), ("pylint", "C0321")},

    {("pylint", "C0326"), ("pycodestyle", "E251")},
    {("pylint", "C0301"), ("pycodestyle", "E501")},
    {("pylint", "W0301"), ("pycodestyle", "E703")},
    {("pylint", "C0321"), ("pycodestyle", "E702")},
    {("pylint", "W0311"), ("pycodestyle", "E111")},
    {("pylint", "W0401"), ("pyflakes", "W0401")},
    {("pydocstyle", "D100"), ("pylint", "C0111")},
)

DUPLICATES: Dict[Tuple[str, str], Set[Tuple[str, str]]] = defaultdict(set)
for group in _DUPLICATE_GROUPS:
    for key in group:
        DUPLICATES[key].update(set(group) - {key})


class Error:
    """Store error information from a linter."""

    __slots__ = ("source", "col", "lnum", "etype", "message", "filename", "number")

    def __init__(
        self,
        source: str = "pylama",
        col: int = 1,
        lnum: int = 1,
        type: str | None = None,
        text: str = "unknown error",
        filename: str = "",
        number: str = "",
        **_,
    ):
        text = str(text).strip().replace("\n", " ")
        if not number:
            match = PATTERN_NUMBER.match(text)
            number = match.group(1).upper() if match else ""
        self.number = number
        self.etype = type[:1] if type else (number[:1] if number else "E")
        self.col = max(int(col or 1), 1)
        self.filename = str(filename)
        self.source = source
        self.lnum = int(lnum or 1)
        self.message = text

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        return self.message

    @property
    def type(self) -> str:
        return self.etype

    def __getitem__(self, key: str) -> Any:
        return self.to_dict()[key]

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"<Error:{self.lnum}:{self.col}: {self.number} {self.message}>"

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.filename}:{self.lnum}:{self.col}: {self.number} {self.message} ({self.source})"

    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        if not isinstance(other, Error):
            return NotImplemented
        return (
            self.filename,
            self.lnum,
            self.col,
            self.number,
            self.message,
            self.etype,
            self.source,
        ) == (
            other.filename,
            other.lnum,
            other.col,
            other.number,
            other.message,
            other.etype,
            other.source,
        )

    def format(self, pattern: str) -> str:
        return pattern.format(
            filename=self.filename,
            lnum=self.lnum,
            col=self.col,
            message=self.message,
            text=self.message,
            etype=self.etype,
            type=self.etype,
            source=self.source,
            number=self.number,
        )

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "source": self.source,
            "col": self.col,
            "lnum": self.lnum,
            "etype": self.etype,
            "type": self.etype,
            "message": self.message,
            "text": self.message,
            "filename": self.filename,
            "number": self.number,
        }


def remove_duplicates(errors: Iterable[Error]) -> List[Error]:
    """Filter duplicate errors reported by multiple linters."""
    unique: List[Error] = []
    passed: DefaultDict[Tuple[str, int], Set[Tuple[str, str]]] = defaultdict(set)
    for error in errors:
        location = (error.filename, error.lnum)
        key = (error.source, error.number)
        if key in passed[location]:
            continue
        if key in DUPLICATES and passed[location] & DUPLICATES[key]:
            continue
        passed[location].add(key)
        unique.append(error)
    return unique


def default_sorter(err: Error) -> Any:
    """Sort by line number."""
    return err.lnum
